title: The Collected Letters of Samuel Taylor Coleridge (6 volumes)
reliability_notes: The standard scholarly Coleridge correspondence, Oxford, 1956-1971, dating and authenticating the letters with manuscript readings; the usual basis for the chronology of his life and career. It is not the fabricated 'Cambridge Edition' of the letters, which does not exist.

title: Blackwood's Edinburgh Magazine
author_or_editor: Founded and published by William Blackwood in 1817; principal editors included John Gibson Lockhart and William Maginn
reliability_notes: The great Tory-Covenanting Edinburgh monthly, the venue for Hogg, Lockhart and the 'Noctes Ambrosianae' and a main organ of the Romantic-era magazine culture. Launched as the Edinburgh Monthly Magazine in 1817 before relaunching under Blackwood's name; cite individual numbers by volume and date.

title: The Edinburgh Review
author_or_editor: Founded October 1802 by Francis Jeffrey, Sydney Smith, Francis Horner and Henry Brougham; edited by Francis Jeffrey from 1803
reliability_notes: The Whig review that defined Romantic-era criticism and shaped the reception of Wordsworth, Byron and the Lake poets; Jeffrey's editorship (1803-1829) makes it central to installments covering British Romanticism. Imprints changed over the run, so cite by volume and date.

title: The Quarterly Review
author_or_editor: Founded March 1809 by the publisher John Murray; first edited by William Gifford
reliability_notes: The Tory counterweight to the Edinburgh Review, the hostile venue for famous attacks on Keats, Shelley and others; essential for the contemporary reception history of the period. Continue attributions remain debated, so cite by volume and date.

title: The Examiner
author_or_editor: Founded 1808 by Leigh Hunt and John Hunt; edited by Leigh Hunt
reliability_notes: The radical weekly that championed the 'Cockney' school and published Keats, Shelley and Hazlitt early; a key source for the politics and literary debates of 1808-1832. Published by John Hunt at the Examiner Office.
